{++ Quite physics-oriented. Need to give a longer introduction for most instructors. ++}
Talk about quantities relating to force, energy, power, battery storage, transmission line capacity, and CO_2_ production.

Energy is force*distance. What are some units of energy? (e.g. Voltage-Amp-hour, bbl water, Kwh)
power is energy per unit time. In what units should we measure the capacity of electric transmission lines. (Voltage-Amp-hours/hour, that is, Voltage-Amps)

How would you measure the power produced by a horse (horsepower)?

How much CO_2_ (in kg) is produced by burning a liter of gasoline? Gasoline hydrocarbons have 4 to 12 carbon atoms. How much of the mass of gasoline is contributed by the carbon atoms, how much by the hydrogen. (Molecular weight of carbon is 12, of hydrogen is 1. Figure 2 hydrogen atoms per carbon atom. So, carbon is about 12/14 of the mass of gasoline.) What's the difference between the mass of CO_2_ and the mass of carbon generated by burning a liter of gasoline.

How many cars are on the road in the US. What's a typical distance driven? What's a typical fuel economy (liters / 100 km)? How much gasoline is consumed in a year? How much CO_2_ is produced in a year?


:::
